title: High-Performance Branch-Free Algorithms for Extended-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic
problem: Existing algorithms for extended-precision floating-point arithmetic (double, triple, quadruple precision) either use complex branching logic or are only correct on specific input classes, limiting performance and generality.
motivation: Extended-precision arithmetic is critical for scientific computing and numerical analysis, but current implementations are slow. Branch-free algorithms could improve performance, particularly on modern CPUs and GPUs.
method: New branch-free algorithms for double, triple, and quadruple precision floating-point arithmetic with computer-verified correctness proofs for all IEEE floating-point inputs (within overflow/underflow thresholds).
key_novelty: Optimal branch-free algorithms with formal correctness proofs, achieving order-of-magnitude speedups over existing libraries.
contributions: Computer-verified correctness proofs for all IEEE inputs
Conjectured to be optimal in FLOP count and circuit depth
General applicability across all input classes
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Detailed algorithm descriptions not available. Hardware-specific optimizations not detailed.
primary_theme: Branch-free extended-precision floating-point algorithms with formal verification
